question: What is the chemical effect that occurs in a battery during the charging process of a Lead Acid battery?

options.text: Lead reacts with sulphur to form lead sulphate
Sulphuric acid dissociates into hydrogen and sulphate ions
Water dissociation into hydrogen and oxygen
Lead sulphate decomposes into lead and sulphuric acid

solution:
__**Lead Acid Battery**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7efd34b8b4390c2c7ab2a6464a70db9030bcbb4e8b99ea0267fe66fe5a18f9de.png] 

__
 
• The battery uses spongy lead and lead peroxide for the conversion of chemical energy into electrical power; such a type of battery is called a lead-acid battery.
 
• The lead-acid battery is most commonly used in power stations and substations because it has a higher cell voltage and a lower cost. It is a reversible battery.

**Explanation**__

**What happens during charging:**

 
• An external DC supply is applied. The chemical reaction is reversed.
 
• Lead sulphate breaks down, and Sulphuric acid is regenerated.
 
• **This means lead sulphate decomposes into lead, lead dioxide, and sulphuric acid.**

**​

What happens during discharging:**

 
• Both positive plate (PbO₂) and negative plate (Pb) convert into lead sulphate (PbSO₄)
 
• Sulphuric acid concentration decreases, and water content increases.
 
• A battery delivers electrical energy.
